poster_title: EduIllustrate: Towards Scalable Automated Generation Of Multimodal Educational Content
authors: Shuzhen Bi, Mingzi Zhang, Zhuoxuan Li, Xiaolong Wang, Keqian Li, Aimin Zhou
paper_info: 2025, A benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interleaved text-diagram explanation generation for K-12 STEM problems

content: Evaluation of LLMs in education has primarily focused on question-answering and tutoring tasks.
Coordinating visual diagrams with textual reasoning reduces cognitive burden and deepens conceptual understanding in K-12 education.
Producing such materials at scale is a significant challenge due to the time-consuming nature of lesson planning and the specialized skills required for accurate diagrams.
Lack of benchmarks to measure LLMs' ability to generate coherent, diagram-rich explanations for K-12 STEM problems.
Existing benchmarks do not jointly assess textual and visual quality of educational content.
panels.headline: Evaluation of LLMs in education has primarily focused on question-answering and tutoring tasks.

content: Curated a problem set of 230 K-12 STEM problems spanning five subjects and three grade levels.
Standardized generation protocol with sequential anchoring to ensure cross-diagram visual consistency.
8-dimension evaluation rubric grounded in multimedia learning theory to assess both text and visual quality.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of EduIllustrate. Given a K-12 STEM problem, the generation protocol produces a structured explanation document through four stages. The resulting output is evaluated using an 8-dimension rubric validated against human expert raters.
panels.headline: Curated a problem set of 230 K-12 STEM problems spanning five subjects and three grade levels.

content: Evaluated ten LLMs using the EduIllustrate benchmark.
Conducted ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of sequential anchoring.
Performed human evaluation with 20 expert raters to validate LLM-as-judge reliability.
panels.figure_caption: Screenshot of the problem review interface used during human annotation. Annotators evaluated each candidate problem against the three curation criteria and recorded their decisions with justifications.
panels.headline: Evaluated ten LLMs using the EduIllustrate benchmark.

content: Gemini 3.0 Pro Preview led the performance at 87.8%.
Sequential anchoring improved Visual Consistency by 13% at 94% lower cost.
panels.figure_caption: Radar charts of all 10 models. (a) By dimension: 8 evaluation dimensions. (b) By subject: overall scores on each of the five subjects. (c) By grade level: overall scores at each grade level.
panels.headline: Gemini 3.0 Pro Preview led the performance at 87.8%.

content: Human evaluation confirmed high reliability for objective dimensions (ρ ≥ 0.83).
Limitations in subjective visual assessment were revealed.
Sequential anchoring significantly improves visual consistency while reducing costs.
Cost vs. quality trade-off analysis shows Kimi-K2.5 offers the best cost-efficiency among high-quality models, achieving 80.8% at $0.12/problem.
Per-stage cost breakdown across ten models indicates Scene Rendering is the most costly stage.

panels.headline: Human evaluation confirmed high reliability for objective dimensions (ρ ≥ 0.83) but revealed limitations in subjective visual assessment.

content: EduIllustrate provides a robust benchmark for evaluating LLMs in generating multimodal educational content for K-12 STEM problems.
Sequential anchoring significantly improves visual consistency while reducing costs.
Subjective visual assessment by LLMs still has limitations.
The benchmark focuses on static diagrams, not dynamic or interactive content.
Future work will explore dynamic and interactive content generation.
